title: Refactor embeddings SDK: paginated streaming, typed responses, and resilient retries
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Motivation: Customer teams are hitting two operational pain points when using the embeddings and reranking endpoints: 1) large result sets (search+rerank workflows) cause high memory/latency when the SDK buffers whole responses, and 2) transient network errors and partial failures result in ambiguous error shapes across Python and TS clients, making retries and typed handling brittle.

Goal: Deliver a cross-language SDK refactor that supports: paginated server-driven result windows (cursor-based), optional streaming of embedding batches for low-latency consumption, consistent typed response models (TypeScript interfaces and Python dataclasses/TypedDicts), and a resilient retry/backoff strategy with idempotency guidance. The work should preserve existing compatibility for small responses and provide migration guidance and migration helpers for customers with minimal code changes.
acceptance_criteria: TS and Python SDKs expose a unified paginated API: client.list_embeddings(cursor=..., limit=...) and an async streaming iterator for very large responses.
Typed responses: TypeScript definitions published to npm; Python provides TypedDict/dataclass models and runtime validation hooks in debug builds.

Retry semantics: network-related 5xx and transient connection errors are retried with exponential backoff and jitter by default; idempotency keys are surfaced for users to opt-in for safe retries of non-idempotent calls.
Backward compatible: existing single-call embeddings() helper continues to work for <100 items; library logs a deprecation path when customers exceed recommended response sizes.

Benchmarks: end-to-end median latency on 1k-item rerank payload reduced by at least 25% in streaming mode versus baseline; memory footprint for client process reduced by at least 50% when using streaming iterator.
Docs: migration guide, code samples (Python/TS), and API reference updated; changelog entry and a short video walkthrough recorded.
E2E tests: coverage for pagination, streaming, type assertions, and retry logic included in CI; integration test against staging embeddings service with injected transient failures.
work_items: Design pagination contract with backend: cursor format, max window, and eviction semantics
Implement server-side cursor support (coord with ENG-8876) and add header-based pagination metadata
TS SDK: add streaming async iterator (for Node 16+), generate type definitions, add retry middleware
Python SDK: add generator-based streaming (async and sync), provide typed models and optional runtime validation
Telemetry: emit spans and counters for page boundaries, retries, and dropped items
Docs & migration guide + examples for migrating from buffered to streaming patterns
Benchmarks and CI integration tests with deterministic failure injection
notes: Trade-offs discussed 2026-02-20: prefer server-driven cursors to avoid client-side state machine complexity; trade is extra round-trips for small page sizes but better stability for large responses.
Opted to make streaming opt-in to avoid surprising existing users and to keep default ergonomics simple.
Considered array-chunking on client but rejected due to duplicated CPU work and inconsistent memory profiles across runtimes.
Security note: cursors are opaque tokens; backend will scope tokens to project/account and short TTL to prevent replay. No PII in cursor payloads.
Open question: Should we expose an 'auto-batch' helper that switches between buffered and streaming based on observed response size? MVP will document pattern but postpone implementation.
